Advances: specled.compiler_tracer.merge_on_flush

Found by the elixir-test-critic during specled_-zr6 verification (2026-07-25). The merge_edges property (test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs:241-293) asserts value provenance only for session-module callers. For a caller present in BOTH previous and session_edges whose module is NOT in session_set (~21% of generated draws), no assertion pins which value wins — mutants reversing Map.merge precedence or concatenating callee lists instead of replacing survived 2000 property cases. The state is production-reachable: during a parallel compile, module B's flush sees module A's fresh edges via session_edges() before A's :on_module fires and marks it a session module (lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex:183-209). Impact bounded — A's own later flush corrects the manifest — so exposure is transient intermediate manifests. Cheapest fix: one example test asserting the session_edges entry wins over a same-key previous entry when the caller's module is not in session_set. Pre-existing; NOT introduced or worsened by specled_-zr6.

ADMISSION VERIFICATION (specled_-k6s, 2026-07-27)
Cold fresh-context verifier run against the epic base tree (feat/specled_-td7-self-identifying-descriptors @ e81f9f98).

VERDICT: still_applicable   EFFORT: trivial
Mandate confirmed still applicable as written; no narrowing needed.

== SCOPED REMAINING WORK ==
All of it. Add one example test to /Users/mz/src/specled_ex-self-identifying-descriptors/test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs inside the existing `describe "Tracer.merge_edges/3 (specled.compiler_tracer.merge_on_flush)"` block (starts line 198, ends line 295), tagged `@tag spec: "specled.compiler_tracer.merge_on_flush"`.

End state — the test must construct a caller whose module is NOT in `session_set` and that is present in BOTH maps with different callee lists, e.g.:

  previous = %{{ModOverlap, :f, 1} => [{String, :old_callee, 1}]}
  session_edges = %{{ModOverlap, :f, 1} => [{String, :upcase, 1}]}
  merged = Tracer.merge_edges(previous, MapSet.new([]), session_edges)
  assert merged[{ModOverlap, :f, 1}] == [{String, :upcase, 1}]

The assertion must be exact list equality (not `Enum.member?`/subset), so it kills BOTH mutants named in the ticket: reversing the `Map.merge(previous_kept, session_edges)` argument order at tracer.ex:299 (would yield `[{String, :old_callee, 1}]`) and concatenating instead of replacing (would yield `[{String, :old_callee, 1}, {String, :upcase, 1}]` after canonicalization). Use module atoms not already bound to other meanings in the file (`ModKeep`, `ModRecompiled`, `ModNew`, `ModA..ModD` are taken).

Optional strengthening (equivalent mandate, higher cost): add a fourth assertion family to the property at tracer_test.exs:241 — for `{caller, callees} <- merged` where the caller's module is NOT in `session_set` and `Map.has_key?(session_edges, caller)`, assert `callees == session_edges |> Map.fetch!(caller) |> Enum.sort() |> Enum.dedup()`. The example test alone satisfies the ticket; do not do both.

No production-code change is required — the implementation is already correct.

== EXPECTED TOUCHES ==
test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs

== RISK NOTES ==
- No realization-hash impact. .spec/realization_hashes.json contains exactly one top-level key, "api_boundary", and no entry names SpecLedEx.Compiler.Tracer or any tracer_test binding; the change is test-only and touches no lib/ file.
- No spec text change required, so no requirement-id collision with other tickets in the set. `specled.compiler_tracer.merge_on_flush` (.spec/specs/compiler_tracer.spec.md:63-73) is not touched by any other ticket in the set (checked all 21 sibling descriptions; none names compiler_tracer, tracer.ex, or tracer_test.exs). Zero file-region conflicts.
- The new tag `@tag spec: "specled.compiler_tracer.merge_on_flush"` is already an existing requirement id and is already covered by an `execute: true` tagged_tests verification entry (.spec/specs/compiler_tracer.spec.md:262-267), so the test-tag-consistency gate in `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` stays green with no spec edit. Adding a NEW tag id would break it; do not invent one.
- No ordering dependency on any other ticket in the set; can land first or last.
- Latent trap for the implementer: `Map.merge/2` argument-order mutants are invisible to every existing assertion because `Enum.reject` at tracer.ex:298 pre-removes session-module collisions. If the implementer "verifies" the new test by mutating the code, the mutation must be at tracer.ex:299 with a non-session collision fixture, or it will appear to pass.
- Spec-prose adjacency (do NOT fold in without a separate ticket): the requirement statement at .spec/specs/compiler_tracer.spec.md:65-71 says "unioned with the session's accumulated edges" and never states which side wins on key collision. The ticket's mandate is a test, not a spec edit; changing the requirement text would touch a `must`/`evolving` requirement and pull this out of trivial effort.

SCOPE CONTRACT (orchestrator, specled_-k6s — 2026-07-27)

Authoritative for mechanical scope checks. Supplements, does not replace, the
ADMISSION VERIFICATION comment's mandate, which is what you implement.

## Out of Scope (intent)

  explicit: "The example test alone satisfies the ticket; do not do both."
- The assertion must be EXACT LIST EQUALITY — not `Enum.member?`, not a subset check.
  That is what kills both mutants; a membership check kills neither cleanly.
- Use module atoms not already bound in the file. `ModKeep`, `ModRecompiled`, `ModNew`,
  and `ModA`..`ModD` are taken.
- No new dependencies.

## FALSIFIABILITY BAR — this ticket is one of the five the epic gates on
The whole point is that the existing property has no value-provenance assertion. Prove
your new test kills BOTH named mutants:
1. Reverse the `Map.merge(previous_kept, session_edges)` argument order in
   `lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex` → the test must go RED (it would yield the
   previous callee list).
2. Concatenate instead of replacing → the test must go RED (it would yield both callees
   after canonicalization).
3. Revert both, confirm green.
Paste both red outputs into your completion record and record the mutations and reverts
in the COMMIT MESSAGE.

## Verification (change-scoped, run-until-green; host mix, no compose)
1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/compiler/tracer_test.exs`
3. `mix format --check-formatted`
4. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`
5. `git diff --name-only` must list exactly one file, and must NOT list
   `lib/specled_ex/compiler/tracer.ex`.

Do NOT run bare `mix spec.check` and do NOT run the full suite. Note this file is
`async: false` and mutates the shared `_build/<env>/.spec` manifest — do not run its
tests concurrently with a compile of the same `_build`.
